title: Draft branches without pages
brief: Compare five document-native ways to switch between Current, named drafts, pinned versions, and a continuous timeline as quickly as changing pages—then review and merge a draft without making Git the user-facing dependency.
defaultWhy: Branch Switcher is the AI recommendation at 91.6/100: it makes the daily Current ↔ Draft move as direct as the familiar page menu while retaining a quiet route to versions and a deliberate handoff to the stronger Changes Navigator review surface.
decisionHinge: The recommendation assumes that rapid personal experimentation is more common than resolving conflicts. If merge review is the daily task, move 10 points from fast switching to cross-depth review; Changes Navigator rises from 83.4 to 87.4 but still needs the Switcher as its entry point.
invariants: One SystemSketch document exposes 1 durable canvas; Frames and Depth Stack stay structural/navigation tools, never branch containers.
Every named Draft records its precise Current v0.7 or pinned-Version base and leaves Current unchanged while edited.
Pinned Versions are immutable/read-only; restoring or branching makes a new editable head rather than rewriting history.
A merge validates the base and pauses for an explicit resolution when Current and Draft touched the same item.
Git may be used underneath if it earns its keep, but the user never needs a repository, branch checkout, or commit to sketch.
boundary: The gallery uses realistic SystemSketch-style chrome and interactive local mock state. It does not change the application, tldraw records, local files, page model, or Git state; snapshot storage, record-aware diffing, and merge execution are deliberately simulated.

requirements.name: Switch states as quickly as pages
requirements.why: The everyday job is opening Current or a named experiment without turning document history into a separate workspace.
requirements.passCondition: From the top-right control, a user can identify and switch to Current or a draft in one deliberate action.

anchors.1: State switching requires a modal workflow or a separate browser surface.
anchors.3: States are reachable but require hierarchy or search to recover.
anchors.5: Current and drafts are immediately scannable and switch with the muscle memory of a page picker.

requirements.name: Keep continuous history useful
requirements.why: Pinned versions and a continuous timeline make experimental work recoverable even when it is never merged.
requirements.passCondition: A user can find a named version or earlier point, inspect it read-only, and branch safely from it.

anchors.1: Only named drafts are visible; ordinary history is hidden.
anchors.3: Versions and recent activity exist but require a secondary route.
anchors.5: A chronological history clearly relates versions, draft roots, and merges.

requirements.name: Make Current versus Draft unmistakable
requirements.why: A prototype must never feel like it is quietly editing the official board.
requirements.passCondition: The selected state, editability, base, and safe return to Current are clear at a glance.

anchors.1: Users infer state from filenames or memory.
anchors.3: State is labeled but disappears while editing.
anchors.5: The active state and Draft mode are continuously visible, and Current remains recoverable.

requirements.name: Review and merge across nested changes
requirements.why: A branch can alter root wiring and a deeply stepped-in Block; a raw whole-board diff cannot make both reviewable.
requirements.passCondition: Before Current changes, the user can navigate each change in context and resolve a real conflict deliberately.

anchors.1: Promotion replaces Current wholesale or shows raw JSON.
anchors.3: A before/after view exists but deep changes must be found manually.
anchors.5: A change list drives focused navigation and conflicts offer explicit source/target choices.

requirements.name: Fit SystemSketch without Git ceremony
requirements.why: Git ideas are useful implementation inspiration, but local sketching should not require a repository, commits, or checkout vocabulary.
requirements.passCondition: The user can draft, pin, switch, and merge in an ordinary local document with no Git prerequisite.

anchors.1: The workflow exposes branches, commits, and working trees as required concepts.
anchors.3: Git is optional but dominates navigation.
anchors.5: The UI is document-native; any Git-backed storage remains an invisible implementation choice.

hardGates.name: No pages as draft branches
hardGates.why: SystemSketch has one durable canvas; drafts are document revisions, not tldraw pages.

hardGates.name: Every Draft has a recorded base
hardGates.why: A Draft begins at a visible Current version or named Version, never at an ambiguous moving state.

hardGates.name: No blind promotion
hardGates.why: A base check and explicit conflict stop are required before Current can change.

hardGates.name: No Git prerequisite
hardGates.why: Version-control ideas may shape implementation, but standalone sketching must remain document-native.

variants.name: Branch Switcher
variants.thesis: Turn the former page-picker location into one compact Current / Drafts / Versions list; switching is instant, while merging enters a focused review.
variants.bestWhen: Most work is personal prototyping and the common action is flipping between Current and two or three named alternatives.
variants.losesWhen: The user spends most of the session comparing long histories or resolving many individual conflicts.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: A named Draft rooted at Current.

decisions.label: Everyday interaction
decisions.value: One page-picker-like popover and one click to switch.

decisions.label: Merge
decisions.value: Draft mode hands off to a separate change-review surface.

proof: The top-right Versions & drafts control and each primary action toggle real local gallery state.
All variants render the same Current v0.7 → safer-ingress Draft scenario with a root safety gate and one depth-2 label change.
This is a standalone interaction prototype: document serialization, version storage, and merge execution remain simulated.

story.title: Switch between the official board and a draft

steps.label: Read the state list
steps.caption: Current, two Drafts, their bases, and their change counts sit in the one top-right popover.

steps.label: Open the draft
steps.caption: The amber Draft bar and the changed Safety gate make the state change impossible to miss.

fr1.evidence: The mock presents Current and both Drafts together in the top-right list; the live control switches the complete canvas state.

fr2.evidence: Versions are one click away from the same popover, but chronology is intentionally not the first thing shown.

fr3.evidence: Current and Draft use separate row treatments and Draft mode persists above the board.

fr4.evidence: A draft has a clear Review merge handoff and change count, but detailed per-change review lives in another surface.

fr5.evidence: It uses only Current, Draft, Version, and Review; there is no Git vocabulary or setup.

g1.evidence: The mock preserves SystemSketch's measured 1-canvas document rule; all state switches replace the document revision, never a page.

g2.evidence: Each Draft shows a specific Current version or named Version as its base and edits only its own simulated head.

g3.evidence: Merge UI names a base and offers a conflict stop; the mock never silently overwrites Current.

g4.evidence: The interaction uses document terms—Current, Draft, Version, merge—not repository checkout or commit jargon.

variants.name: State Deck
variants.thesis: Make Drafts feel maximally like pages: the top-right control opens visual thumbnail cards for Current and each alternate board state.
variants.bestWhen: The decision is primarily visual and rapid flipping between a few spatially distinct design options matters more than lineage.
variants.losesWhen: Trustworthy continuous history, named versions, and record-level merging must be first-class rather than tucked behind the visual deck.
